messages:
Anya V.: rolling the CUDA 12.1 toolkit to canary us-west-2-gpu-1 pool now. starting with 6 nodes.
Mike L.: heads-up — these nodes are running a mix of gcc12/gcc13 compiled images from last month. watch for PTX/codegen mismatches.
Kevin R.: noted. will keep drain windows short. if we see nvml/driver version mismatch we should auto-fallback to cu11 image.
Anya V.: first node came up, but runtime logs show repeated NCCL TIMEOUT and processes stuck in D-state. pastebin: https://paste.example/abcd1234
Suz (oncall): seeing kernel taints on that node: "NVRM: GPU at PCI:0000:65:00: GPU is lost" then nvidia_uvm unload fails. dmesg attached.
Mike L.: that smells like PTX JIT failure; container images rebuilt with newer toolkit and produced different SASS/PTX cache. did we clear PTX cache?
EngRuntime Team: we rebuilt images during the rollout to include cudnn 9.1 and switched host-compiler flags to -march=sm90 on the canary image. we also updated the base image to ubuntu22.04.
Kevin R.: okay that explains it. older driver (535.x) + new PTX compiled for sm90 can produce unsupported cubin on Ampere nodes with older microcode.
Anya V.: actions: 1) drain 2) label problem_nodes 3) rollback to cu11 fallback image if healthcheck fails 2 consecutive times.
infra-bot: node i-0382a7 marked cordoned by Anya V. (reason: cuda12-canary-fallback)
Mike L.: after cordon, scheduler moved pods; but a lot of long-running workloads hit OOM/redis reconnects because they were EBS-bound and restarted on same AZ. cost impact: 6/6 canary pods in pending/restart => throughput drop on batch jobs.
Suz (oncall): logs show repeated: "nvidia-fabric 0:0: NCCL WARN AllReduce - timeout at 10000ms" and kworker showing stack traces.
Kevin R.: temporary mitigation: set NCCL_MAX_RETRIES=1 and NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=^docker_gwbridge to speed failure/fallback. also reduce NCCL timeout env to 2s to trigger faster fallbacks.
Anya V.: tried that, but network stack between AZs caused long tail; we forced local-scheduling which reduced cross-AZ NCCL traffic and recovered 2 nodes.
Mike L.: we found a subtle problem: container rebuild stripped /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcuda.so symlink to libcuda.so.1. host driver expects SONAME libcuda.so.1, container had libcuda.so -> libcuda.so.2, ldconfig mismatch.
EngRuntime Team: adding: we ship a shim that binds host /usr/lib/libcuda.so.1 into the container at runtime; can push as immediate hotfix.
Anya V.: please push shim to canary image and restart kubelet on the two remaining bad nodes.
Kevin R.: pushed shim as image tag cuda12-hotfix-2026-03-18. command used on daemonset:
```
kubectl set image ds/nvidia-shim nvidia-shim=repo/redwood/cuda12-hotfix-2026-03-18
kubectl rollout restart daemonset/nvidia-shim
```
Mike L.: after shim, uvm unload errors dropped, but we still saw one node with repeated OOMs — turned out the kernel had a weird page allocator fragmentation after the driver reload. clearing GPU caches and reboot fixed it.
Suz (oncall): rebooting a node during business hours hit a burst of customer-facing latency. ops: please coordinate next time with customer-alerts. (reacted :loudspeaker:)
Anya V.: agreed — next canary will use one node at a time and test synthetic large-batch inference for 30m.
EngRuntime Team: we're adding preflight checks to the image build: verify host-driver-compat table, run ldconfig and assert SONAME matches, run small PTX JIT smoke test for available architectures. also creating a container label: redwood.com/cuda-compat=validated.
Kevin R.: long term: we should standardize on an allowed toolchain matrix and add a pre-merge CI job that uses the lowest-driver version we support (e.g., 535.86) to compile kernels. if compiled kernels run on the lowest driver, they should run everywhere.
Mike L.: cost note: canary took ~18h of degraded throughput; batch backlog caused 12% extra cloud GPU hours in us-west-2. finance pinged.
Anya V.: filed rfd to require host-driver pinning on Dedicated pools and to add an automated fallback route in Smart Router when nodes in a region enter "cuda-incompatible" state.
infra-bot: jira issue INFRA-2345 created by Anya V. (title: "cuda12 canary fallback + image preflight")
deploy-bot: rollback of deployment redwood/runtime-canary -> repo/redwood/runtime:2026-03-10 initiated by Anya V.
Suz (oncall): postmortem note: sequence = image rebuild -> PTX change -> libcuda SONAME mismatch -> kernel taint -> NCCL timeouts -> OOM fallout -> customer latency. add runbook item for libcuda shim and one-node canary.
Anya V.: thanks everyone. next steps: EngRuntime to add the preflight, EngInfra to add auto-drain policy on SONAME mismatch, Oncall to update runbook. will reconvene in async thread with updated numbers. :thumbsup:
Mike L.: closing loop: pushed PR to eng-runtime with smoke-tests + ldconfig assertion. request review @Kevin R.
Kevin R.: reviewing now. good job catching, simple fixes for short-term. we'll schedule a full rollback drill next week.
Suz (oncall): logging metric: "cuda.compat.failures" created and alert threshold at 2 nodes/15m.
Anya V.: end of thread — saving logs to INFRA-2345 and pinging finance for cost breakdown.
